headline: Very Strong El Nino -- RONI +1.97 degC (ASO 2026; legacy ONI +2.46), power index 84/100 (Very High), intensifying rapidly.
episode_status: Established El Nino episode: 5 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC (NOAA requires 5).

mjo.note: CPC's newest pentad is 27 days old (25 Oct), too old to say where the active phase is now.

notes: 4 candidate analogs were dropped for being too dissimilar to the current trajectory.

alerts.title: Formal El Nino episode criteria met
alerts.detail: 5 consecutive overlapping seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC, from AMJ 2026. NOAA's five-season rule is satisfied.

alerts.title: Projected to peak in very strong territory
alerts.detail: Ensemble peak +2.28 degC at NDJ 2026, 94% probability of exceeding +2.0 degC.

alerts.title: RONI at or above +2.0 degC - Very strong El Nino
alerts.detail: ASO 2026 RONI is +1.97 degC, which CPC prints as +2.0: Very Strong El Nino conditions this season. An event's category is set by its peak, which is still ahead of it while it is building.

alerts.title: Third-warmest ASO or better
alerts.detail: Rank 2 of 77 for this calendar season on RONI.

alerts.title: Ocean and atmosphere are coupled
alerts.detail: Composite atmospheric index +1.83 sigma, with 90% of indicators in agreement.

alerts.title: Still intensifying
alerts.detail: RONI rose +0.28 degC from the previous season (intensifying rapidly).

alerts.title: East and central Pacific: 2.6x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 359 units of accumulated cyclone energy against 138 for a normal season by 21 November. 25 named storms, 13 hurricanes, 11 major.

alerts.title: Repeated westerly wind forcing over the warm pool
alerts.detail: 6 months in the last year averaged strongly westerly at 850 hPa in the western Pacific, which is how downwelling Kelvin waves get launched.

alerts.title: Legacy ONI and official RONI diverging
alerts.detail: ONI +2.46 against RONI +1.97, a gap of +0.49 degC. That much of the raw anomaly is the whole tropical ocean running warm rather than the Pacific, which is why CPC has classified on RONI since February 2026.

alerts.title: Atlantic: 0.16x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 20 units against 120 normal by 21 November. A suppressed basin is the expected signature of El Nino in the Atlantic, and it is not a reason to relax: 1992 was a quiet season and it produced Andrew.

alerts.title: Westerly wind event under way: east region, 180-150W, 5S-5N
alerts.detail: 48.5 days above +2 m/s since 2026-10-01 06Z in CCMP's near-real-time winds to 2026-11-18, peaking at +10.5 m/s on 2026-11-07; longer than any of the 351 events in Harrison and Vecchi's 1986-1995 list (at most 32.5 days): a sustained westerly anomaly more than a burst. Equatorial westerly anomalies force downwelling Kelvin waves east.

outlook.label: Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast
outlook.text: 1. Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast: A large non-tropical low pressure area centered a few hundred miles east of northeastern Florida continues to produce disorganized showers and thunderstorms. The system is moving into an environment that will probably not be conducive for development of significant tropical or subtropical characteristics. 1. Although the chances of tropical development continue to decrease, this large weather system is still expected to produce gusty winds, dangerous surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week. In addition, heavy rainfall and the threat of flash flooding will move northward over coastal portions of the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic through the weekend. Interests along the U.S. East Coast should continue to monitor the progress of this system. Additional information on this system, including Gale Warnings, can be found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, as well as products issued by your local National Weather Service forecast office. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

outlook.label: Invest 96S
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 96S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 10.4S 90.2E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 10.8S 90.4E, APPROXIMATELY 394 NM WEST OF COCOS ISLANDS. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED (EIR) SATELLITE DEPICTS DEEP CONVECTION DISPLACED BY MODERATE NORTHWESTERLY VERTICAL WIND SHEAR TO THE SOUTHERN PORTION OF AN ELONGATED LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC) EVIDENT IN A 200344Z METOP-C ASCAT PASS. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS A MARGINAL ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH MODERATE VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) OF (10 TO 15 KNOTS), MODERATE TO STRONG POLEWARD UPPER-LEVEL OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (SSTS) OF 28 TO 29 C. GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC MODELS DEPICT A CLEARLY DEFINED CIRCULATION, THOUGH THE SYSTEM STRUGGLES TO MEET WIND SPEED CRITERIA AS IT TRAVERSES SOUTHWARD. ENSEMBLE MODELS DEPICT A SLOW DEVELOPMENT TREND OVER THE NEXT 24-36 HOURS. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 27 TO 32 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1006 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS REMAINS MEDIUM.

outlook.label: Invest 98S
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 98S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 7.7S 75.5E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 7.7S 75.3E, APPROXIMATELY 167 NM EAST OF DIEGO GARCIA. RECENT ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED SATELLITE IMAGERY INDICATES PATCHY DEEP CONVECTION DEVELOPING OVER A DEVELOPING, ELONGATED LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION EVIDENT IN A 201620Z PARTIAL METOP-C ASCAT PASS. THIS DISTURBANCE LIES IN AN AREA OF LOW VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (5-10 KTS), FAVORABLE UPPER-LEVEL OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (29-30C). HOWEVER, THE DEVELOPING CIRCULATION IS STILL QUITE WEAK AND DISORGANIZED, AND DETERMINISTIC MODELS AND ENSEMBLES BOTH INDICATE SLOW DEVELOPMENT OVER THE NEXT FEW DAYS AS THE SYSTEM TRACKS GENERALLY POLEWARD. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 13 TO 18 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1009 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS REMAINS LOW.

outlook.label: Invest 97S
outlook.text: AN AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 97S) HAS PERSISTED NEAR 6.6S 66.3E, APPROXIMATELY 371 NM WEST OF DIEGO GARCIA. RECENT ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS DEEP CONVECTION DEVELOPING OVER A BROAD AREA OF LOW-LEVEL CYCLONIC TURNING EVIDENT IN A 201448Z SSMIS PASS. THIS DISTURBANCE LIES IN A GENERALLY FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT WITH LOW VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (5-10 KTS), MODERATE POLEWARD UPPER-LEVEL OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (29-30C). DETERMINISTIC AND ENSEMBLE MODELS INDICATE SLOW BUT STEADY CONSOLIDATION OF THIS SYSTEM AS IT MEANDERS EASTWARD OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 18 TO 23 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1009 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS LOW.

stormfury.verdict: 1 of 1 live storms fail STORMFURY's own criteria. Every one of them fails on supercooled water, which is the criterion no hurricane has ever passed and the reason the programme ended.
reasons: TRIGGER: the seeding agent needs supercooled liquid water and hurricane eyewalls are already glaciated at seeding altitude. Nothing to freeze, so the mechanism never starts. Willoughby et al., Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 1985.

MAGNITUDE: across 37 natural eyewall expansions in 13 hurricanes this season, conserving angular momentum predicted a mean 28.0% wind drop and the storms actually gave up 4.3%, overstating it 6.5-fold. A hurricane is fed high-momentum air continuously, so a closed-system argument is an upper bound, not a forecast. STORMFURY's predicted effect came from that same calculation.

DETECTION: 29 of 316 unseeded hurricane intervals this season weakened by at least the 31% STORMFURY claimed for Debbie, and 62 moved that far in one direction or the other. An effect that size is indistinguishable from what hurricanes do untouched, which is what closed the programme.

programme.agencies: US Weather Bureau / NOAA with the US Navy

seeded_storms.name: Esther
seeded_storms.outcome: Flown before STORMFURY formally existed, as the proof of concept that got the programme funded.

seeded_storms.name: Beulah
seeded_storms.claimed: eyewall dissipated and reformed further out
seeded_storms.outcome: The first run missed the target area entirely. The second produced the reformation the hypothesis predicted, which is also what an unseeded eyewall replacement looks like.

seeded_storms.name: Debbie
seeded_storms.outcome: The showcase: five seedings on each of two days. These are the numbers the programme is remembered for, and the ones the natural replacement cycle later explained without any silver iodide.

seeded_storms.name: Ginger
seeded_storms.outcome: A large, diffuse storm with no coherent eyewall to move. It was seeded because it was what was available, which is itself a statement about how rarely the criteria above are met.

criteria.name: Within aircraft range
criteria.detail: 9,907 km from Lakeland, Florida, beyond the 2,040 km operational radius assumed here

criteria.name: Coherent eyewall
criteria.detail: 40 kt is below the 64 kt hurricane threshold; there is no closed eyewall to relocate

criteria.name: Clear of land for 24 h
criteria.detail: official track stays 494 km off the coast; no ensemble on file, so this is the deterministic track alone

criteria.name: Supercooled water to seed
criteria.detail: Hurricane eyewall updrafts are largely glaciated by the time they reach those temperatures. Warm-rain coalescence removes liquid water below the freezing level efficiently enough that little survives to be supercooled, leaving the seeding agent with nearly nothing to act on. The trigger is absent. The mechanism cannot start.

atlas.method: Past El Ninos (RONI >= +1.0) minus neutral years (|RONI| < 0.5), per season, per grid cell, since 1979, with each event and each neutral year counted once. Welch's t accompanies every difference and is judged against each season's own 95% point of Student's t. An event under way when the grids were built is left out.

cpc_discussion.synopsis: El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance).
cpc_discussion.body:
Compared to last month, El Nino strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0°C, extending farther westward across the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean [Fig. 1] . The Nino indices increased, reaching +2.5°C in Nino-3.4, +3.6°C in Nino-3, and +4.4°C in Nino-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained significantly above average [Fig. 3] , associated with a deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Convection and rainfall remained enhanced from the central to the eastern Pacific, while suppressed conditions persisted over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were consistently negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected the ongoing evolution of El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will continue to strengthen before beginning to weaken in early 2027 [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Chances for a historic event exceeding previous El Ninos dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ) are now ~60% for the October-December and November-January periods, remaining at better than even odds. Even with a very strong El Nino, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are higher, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance).
